s2-conflicts.summary: 3 hard conflict(s) detected — no silent resolution permitted. Human decision required on: strength vs permeability; ammonium_emission vs pathway; ammonium_emission vs pathway.

conflict_matrix.description: MICP precipitation that raises strength typically clogs pores and reduces permeability by 1–2 orders of magnitude (S11); 'maximize strength' + 'maintain original permeability' is a hard physical trade-off, not an optimization problem. Constraint "strength"="maximize UCS" vs "permeability"="keep original permeability unchanged"
Higher cementation usually needs more treatment cycles / reagent, raising cost; treat as soft unless both are pinned to exact values. Constraint "strength"="maximize UCS" vs "cost"="minimum cost"
Permeability control to tight tolerances requires staged injection and monitoring, increasing cost. Constraint "permeability"="keep original permeability unchanged" vs "cost"="minimum cost"

Ureolytic MICP stoichiometrically produces 2 mol NH₄⁺ per mol urea (S10); 'urea pathway' + 'zero ammonium emission' is contradictory unless an explicit capture/removal step is added — non-urea pathways (S13) must not reuse urea-path models. Constraint "ammonium_emission"="zero NH4 emission" vs "pathway"="urea hydrolysis"

Ureolytic MICP stoichiometrically produces 2 mol NH₄⁺ per mol urea (S10); constraint "pathway"="urea hydrolysis" combined with "ammonium_emission"="zero NH4 emission" is contradictory unless an explicit NH₄⁺ capture/removal step is added — non-urea pathways (S13) must not reuse urea-path models.
